cursor.note: PROVED. An intention can now be marked retired in a shape the gate READS, the reverse read says who is riding it AND what it could not see, and a boat riding a retired intention cannot move forward. Verdict at /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-20260818T194738-1b5e1bb3a84f.json — 8 of 8 criteria pass, 7 hypotheses confirmed, 3 KILLED, deposited to the hypothesize tree. THE THREE KILLS ARE THE PART WORTH READING IN A YEAR. (1) The blind count was predicted at 43/8/0 over 72 boats and measured 40/7/3 over 69 in flight — the hand sweep behind the prediction counted every ticket file and matched brackets by eye. The interesting half is the third number: the corpus has a class the prediction said would be EMPTY. Three tickets carry prose where a bracketed cursor belongs, and their flight status cannot be judged AT ALL. Folding that into 'not riding' would have made three unjudgeable boats read as three boats definitely not riding, so it is reported as its own class. (2) The reverse read does NOT use register._open_boats' rule, and the two populations reconcile exactly rather than agreeing: register calls 162 tickets open because its question is 'has this left the folder'; riders_of finds 69 because its question is 'is this boat still moving'. 162 = 69 + 90 done-but-not-berthed (register's own filed edge (c)) + 3 unjudgeable. (3) The probe's `enough` does not gate on 'the blind count has been non-zero', because that clause is VACUOUS on this corpus — it is already non-zero and would clear the watch on the day it was armed, which is a check going green at the moment its condition is satisfied. The counts ride in every payload instead, and 'acted on' becomes the ticket's own EARLY STOP: enough fires the moment the gate refuses a boat the retiring hand's scan had not listed. AND CRITERION 2's OWN WORDING WAS FALSIFIED, recorded as falsified rather than smoothed: it claimed equality with 'the in-flight boat count register.register() reports', and register reports no such number. The validate berth pre-registered this as unknown #2 — 'if it reds that way, the identity is the finding and the criterion is the thing that was wrong.' THE HOLLOW THIS BUILD FOUND IN ITSELF: Riders.attributable started DERIVED, which made the partition identity true by arithmetic — deleting a blind class raised attributable by exactly as much and every check stayed green. The mutation tooth caught it on its first run. For one commit, 'this report's blindness cannot be removed silently' was a claim about subtraction. It is now a counted field, and the mutation is re-run externally against the file on disk: three classes deleted in turn, exit 1 every time, green control between. ONE WRONG-CONDITION CONTROL IS RECORDED, because it read exactly like a clean negative: the third mutation's first attempt did not apply (a sed pattern assuming a trailing comma the last dict entry does not have) and the suite exited 0. The guard printed PATTERN NOT FOUND beside it and the run was redone. SCOPE HONESTLY SHORT: no intention in the corpus is retired today, so the gate half is proved in fixture and the read half live; the refusal's LIVE half is deliberately claimed by no criterion, and answering it is the probe's job. The 40 unattributed, the 7 remaining unresolvable and the 3 unreadable are REPORTED and left standing — they are the child this ticket names, not this voyage's work.

THE GATE'S QUEUE IS REAL, AND IT CAUGHT THIS VERY CROSSING ON THE FIRST TRY. Six criteria run by their own instruments, five hypotheses confirmed, verdict berthed at verdict-20260810T222204-9239cdda9ed3.json before this crossing.

THE FALSIFIER WAS ANSWERED BY A REAL REFUSAL, NOT A FIXTURE — which is more than the voyage set out to get. The first attempt at this PROVED crossing was REFUSED: Unproven, because retiring the prose IOU had edited voyage.py after the seal, so the component's fingerprint had moved (bdd6a18eafee -> e46b3389d042) and Law 3 had closed the validation's horizon. Before today that refusal would have raised and vanished. Instead the store now holds it, and read_attempts() returns it complete: actor CC, target PROVED, the full workflow string, 2026-08-11T04:22:30Z, reason_type Unproven, and the whole message naming both fingerprints and the fix. Every clause of the ticket's falsifier — who asked, for what transition, when, the REASON, readable afterwards, a grant distinguishable from a refusal — is satisfied by a record the running system made of its own accord, in normal work. asked 2 = granted 1 + refused 1.

WHAT THE VOYAGE SETTLED:

1. THE WRITER'S PLACE WAS A MEASUREMENT. 14 refusal paths reach a caller of the gate and only 7 raise inside the decision function's own text; the other 7 are OwnerUnresolvable out of boat_owner_of, a helper shared with readers that clear nothing. A writer at the raise sites would have looked finished and recorded half the surface. The frame covers all fourteen, so clear() is now a thin public door around a private _decide() — and the first cut, which took **kwargs, erased the keyword-only structure that makes proven_by unsmuggleable. The proof that catches a smuggled witness went red and named it.

2. THE CONSUMER WAS A LAW 7 QUESTION WITH A CODE ANSWER. write_trace reaps consumer='debug' past 30 days on every subsequent write. A record of truth that evaporates is not one — hence 'training', proven by aging a store 400 days and watching a debug record die beside a surviving clearance record.

3. THE READ FACE BELONGS TO THE OWNER, and a second consumer is what proved it. The reader was written in the probe and moved to clearance.read_attempts() the moment voyage.py's [X] marker wanted the same fact: two spellings of one block/event/consumer vocabulary are one drift away from a confident zero (Law 1, Law 6). The probe composes it and only counts.

4. THE MARKERS DID NOT GRAFT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The pre-declared reader filed [R] requested and [X] refused as both waiting on 'the queue'. With the queue built they want different things, and neither wants only data: [R] presumes DWELL, which a synchronous gate has none of — it waits on a design question nobody has asked. [X] has its fact but needs 'still refused since the last journaled crossing', without which the flag pins on the first refusal and fires on normal motion. Each says so at its own entry now, and the blanket header sentence that went on asserting the store did not exist is gone. It fired the acceptance instrument RED first, which is how it was caught: one sentence covering a set that had stopped being uniform is how a filed absence outlives the voyage that filled it.

5. THE EVIDENCE IS PROTECTED FROM ITS OWN PROOFS. Both harbor_master proofs redirect CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT process-wide at import and assert the live file came out byte-identical. A counted fixture refusal would not be a messy file; it would be manufactured evidence that the gate once stood in a real crossing's way. The refusal above is genuine precisely because no proof can reach that file.

6. REPAIRED IN PASSING: test_harbor_asks_the_real_host.py had not been re-run since boat-owner-is-read-not-stated ruled this morning. It still handed the gate a boat_owner (now refused outright) alongside an invented boat id with no ticket on disk. It names a real cast boat now and reads the owner off it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: two records is not a rate. The ticket's horizon — does a refusal repeat often enough to need damping, the way the trouble lane damps? — stays open, and the shape of the first refusal is a data point rather than an answer. Notably it argues for the ACTOR-and-code side rather than the boat: this refusal was about a stale fingerprint, a condition that clears the moment the proof is re-run, which is exactly the 'refused once then moving' case that would pin a naive [X].

window.note: BUILDME. Charted whole before a byte moved: orient -> constrain -> survey -> decompose -> triage -> hypothesize -> validate, seven berths under ticket a-superseded-intention-is-never-silent, validate at validate-20260818T192832-e2bd14803222.json. THE DESIGN QUESTION THE CHART SETTLED: ruling.supersede() already solves supersession in this corpus, and it puts the state on the SUCCESSOR (append to its `supersedes` list) precisely so the retired packet — carrying Akien's signature — is never touched. That inversion does not transfer here. A charter is an authored design record that has always grown by addition, not a signed confirmation; carrying the state on the successor would cost a 59-file scan inside every crossing for a state that is almost always absent; and a deprecation with NO successor would be inexpressible. So the key lands on the SUPERSEDED charter as an added top-level key (successor nullable, when, evidence), and what DOES transfer from the ruling door is the discipline: evidence required, normalise on READ never by rewrite, refuse with every reason at once. THE SEAT WAS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN: boat_owner_of already parses the owning intention's charter to read gated_by, so the supersession read is one more .get on a dict in hand — literally 'one more field, not a new lookup' — and _decide's existing ladder means the refusal raises before emit is reached, while clear()'s frame-level tracer records it for free. This build adds no tracing. THREE MEASUREMENTS THE SWEEP TOOK THAT THE TICKET DID NOT HAVE. (1) The ticket's own numbers are wrong: 29 in-flight boats carry owning_intention and 43 do not, not 28/44 — one ticket filed between two counts on the same day, which is the argument for a report that recomputes rather than quotes. (2) A THIRD BLINDNESS CLASS the falsifier does not name: 8 of the 29 attributed boats name an intention address that does not RESOLVE under either root, so a string-matched reverse read would count them as attributed to intentions that do not exist — invisible in the worst direction. The report therefore carries three counters, not one. (3) One of those eight broken addresses is MINE, written today, hours after I read the resolution rule — which is the case for the check being physics rather than for one more careful hand. SEQUENCING TRAP, NAMED IN THE ORDER: harbor_master has ZERO clearable proofs right now — test_clearance's horizon has closed — and this build edits test_clearance, so a fresh seal sits on the critical path to being able to cross PROVED at all. It is piece 7 of 10, after all code and before the probe. OUT OF BOUNDS AND STAYING OUT: backfilling the 43 unattributed tickets (the ticket's named child — doing the chore here would erase the evidence that the declaration was needed), the 41 charters lacking gated_by, and DECIDING what happens to a boat found riding a superseded intention. The mechanism refuses and reports; ending or re-parenting the boat is the owner's act (Law 6).

window.note: PROVEME. cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py — 41 arms, GREEN TWICE (2026-08-18), nine of them new for this ticket. THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS BUILD SETTLED, and it inverts the prior art: ruling.supersede puts the link on the SUCCESSOR because a retired ruling packet is SIGNED and may never be touched. A charter is not signed — it is an authored record that grows by addition — so the retirement key lives on the SUPERSEDED charter, added beside the standing prose rather than rewritten into it (the ticket's second wrong-shape). Three measurements killed the successor-carries-it inversion: a successorless deprecation would be inexpressible; the successor-side read costs a 59-charter scan per crossing; and the gate's seat ALREADY HOLDS the superseded charter's dict. What DID transfer from the ruling door is the discipline — evidence required, normalise on READ never by rewrite, refuse naming every lack at once. THE SEAT IS MEASURED FREE, not asserted: test_a_retirement_is_read_off_the_charter counts builtins.open calls and asserts a retired and a living charter both cost exactly 2 — the refusal reads one more FIELD, not one more FILE. AND THIS BUILD ADDED NO TRACING OF ITS OWN, also measured: an ast census asserts the trace store has exactly one writer (_trace_attempt) called from exactly one place (clear), whose frame-level try/except BaseException already records every refusal that leaves the function — 'including refusals nobody has thought of yet'. A refusal writing its own trace would be a second record of the same fact. THE MUTATION TOOTH CAUGHT A REAL HOLLOW IN MY OWN DESIGN ON ITS FIRST RUN: Riders.attributable was a DERIVED property (in_flight - unattributed - unresolvable), so deleting a whole blind class raised attributable by exactly as much and the partition identity stayed true BY ARITHMETIC — the blind count could have been removed with every proof still green. attributable is now a COUNTED field incremented in the walk, and the tooth reds if any blind class is dropped. That is the ticket's own failure shape (a green earned by not looking) found inside the instrument built to forbid it. THE NUMBERS, AND MY HAND-COUNT WAS WRONG: the ticket's falsifier quotes my pre-build sweep, '28 boats with 44 invisible'. The instrument measures 69 in flight, 21 attributable, 40 unattributed, 8 unresolvable, 3 UNREADABLE. The sweep neither filtered to in-flight nor parsed workflows. Hypothesis 3 predicted 43/8/0 and is PARTIALLY KILLED — the unreadable class is 3, not 0 (a-judge-declares-its-attendance, the-postman-rides, the-route-sieves-carve-out-of-inference-domain all carry prose where a cursor belongs), and a state that cannot be judged is a third kind of blindness I had not predicted. It is reported as its own class rather than folded into 'not riding'. THE REFUSAL IS A WALL, NOT A GATE: IntentionRetired stops FORWARD crossings only; a retreat is exempt, because a retreat is how such a boat gets dealt with, and the gate decides nothing beyond the refusal (Law 6 — ending or re-parenting the boat is the owner's act). A malformed retirement key RAISES RetirementUnreadable and is never collapsed into 'not retired' (Law 7). SCOPE HONESTLY SHORT: the refusal's LIVE half is not claimed by any criterion — no intention in the corpus is retired today, so the gate half is proved by substituting the owner read, and the read half is proved on real files through injected roots. The proof says so in a section header rather than blurring the two.

Probe armed at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/probes/a_superseded_intention_is_never_silent.py — smoke-fired: 56 charters walked, 0 retirements, 0 escapes, 0 refusals, trigger FALSE, enough FALSE. That is the correct resting state on the day the mechanism ships and nothing has used it yet, and it is a MEASUREMENT rather than an assumption: the walk ran, the queue was read, and the zeros are what it found. THREE TRIGGER CLAUSES, each a clause of the ticket's falsifier: (a) an ESCAPE — a forward journaled crossing at or after a retirement's own `when`, by a boat that NAMES the retired intention; (b) an UNREADABLE retirement — a charter that looks retired to a human and is not retired to the gate; (c) a refusal on a boat the retiring hand's scan had NOT listed, which is the ticket's EARLY STOP because it converts the unattributed backlog from a chore into the next build. THE BLIND COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A TRIGGER CLAUSE: it is non-zero today (40/7/3) and will be for a long time, so a probe firing on it would fire every pulse forever and teach nothing. It rides in every payload instead — a standing condition belongs in the carry, not the trigger. AND THERE IS NO ERA-FLOOR CONSTANT, unlike the sibling clearance_actually_gates: each retirement carries its own `when`, so the floor is per-retirement and READ rather than picked. A crossing before a retirement is not an escape, and the record says so itself.
